title: D-11 (proposed): self-host mk2's FORWARD development as units, starting with D045
description:
Question raised by the user 2026-08-15: why doesn't mk2 model its own modules as units? Answer: through phases 0-9 no deliverable asked for it; D-10 deferred it when the DoD forced the question. Two versions exist and must be kept apart:

RETROACTIVE (rejected, correctly): declaring existing modules units with packs that were never frozen and red evidence never recorded is fabricated history — the exact post-hoc-plausible-chain problem evidence anchoring exists to prevent (machine.md §7).

PROSPECTIVE (not yet decided — this bead): from the next increment forward, run mk2's method on mk2 itself. Each future change is a unit: pack frozen BEFORE implementation, red-before-green evidence recorded as it happens via record_evidence, deviations opened when a review finds a spec conflict and adjudicated by someone other than the implementer, publication gated by the real DoD gates, releases with launch criteria. The tool governs its own next increment — the strongest possible dogfood, and not fabricated.

Tradeoff to decide: every future change becomes slower and more ceremonial (freeze, deviations, per-red/green evidence) — the friction the method imposes on purpose. Worth it only if mk2's remaining work (10 open dispositions, D045 tier model, store perf, and anything after) is substantial enough. Pilot: D045 (assurance tier in the snapshot) is the natural first unit — it's real, bounded, and its own subject matter is the tier matrix.

Decide: (a) adopt prospectively starting with D045 as the pilot unit, or (b) reject with reason and leave D-10 as final. Either way, record as D-11 in DECISIONS.md and update D-10's last bullet.
close_reason: D-11 ADOPTED with named exceptions (DECISIONS.md, 2026-08-17): eight units through mk2's own lifecycle, stop rule never fired; docs/method.md binding.
